To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fatty acid composition and rate of lipid oxidation in liver endoplasmatic reticulum is regulated by the fatty acid composition in the diet.

the dietary lipid composition regulates the fatty acid profile of the liver endoplasminc reticulum, which in turn controls the rate of lipid-peroxidation in vitro, and that the rate of lipid oxidation in vitro is an index of the extent of oxidative damage in vivo.

the fatty acid composition and the rate of lipid oxidation in liver microsomes are dependent on the fatty acids present in the diet, that the rate of oxidation is decreased by phenobarbitone treatment, and that the anti-oxidant alpha-tocopherols decreases lipid oxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the polyunsatured fatty acids (PUFA) in the diet in controlling the rate of lipidperoxidation in the liver endoplsmic reticulum in vivo and in vitro.
the regulation of the rate of lipid oxidation in the liver endoplalmic reticulum.
the regulation of the lipid composition of membranes, and the role of membrane lipid composition in the regulation of cellular processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dietary polyunsaturated fatty acyl chains in the liver endoplamic reticulum are the major determinants of the rate and extent lipid peroxidation and this is a major mechanism for the regulation of the rate and amount of lipid peroxidative reactions.

the fatty acid composition in the diet regulates the composition of the liver microsomal phosphatidylethanolamine, and that this in turn regulates the rate of lipid oxidation in the microsomes in vitro.

the dietary lipid components regulate the fatty acid composition and lipid peroxidase activity of the endoplasmatic reticulum, which may be an important factor controlling lipid peroxidation and the rate and extent in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dietary lipid composition determines the fatty acid composition, the lipid peroxidation and the anti-oxidant capacity of the endoplasmatic reticulum of the liver.

dietary polyunsaturated fatty-acid composition is the major determinant of the fatty acid compositions of membranes, and that the fatty acid compositions in turn determine the susceptibility of membranes to lipid peroxidation and other oxidative processes.

the fatty acid composition and the lipid peroxidation capacity of the liver endo-plasmic reticula from rats fed on different diets are closely related to the fatty acid composition, lipid peroxidation and anti-oxidant capacity of the diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dietary fatty acids regulate the fatty acid composition in liver microsomes and that this is an important factor in regulating lipid peroxidation and its associated toxicity.

the fatty acid composition and content of the liver endolasmic reticulam lipid is determined by the dietary fatty acids, and that this in turn controls the rate and extent to which the endoplasmatic reticulum is subject to lipid peroxidation.
the fatty acid composition in the diet can have a significant influence on the fatty acid profile of the liver ER.
